questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to a beautiful and interesting city with a fun student life. Prague is the perfect city to be an exchange student in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I feel like they were good at sending out emails with information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: emails

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through these reports on mobility online. Someone had lived in Balbinova and recommended it so thats how I got my apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The dorms are very cheap but far away from the city center, so if you want to live more central I'd find a room in an apartment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Living in Balbinova (or any of his other locations) is fun cause it's full of other erasmus students so it's very social and easy to make friends. The landlord is a bit weird and the apartments are by no means luxurious, but they're big and it's a great location. And so fun to live with other students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to get up early the day of registration and be quick to get the courses you wanted. You probably wont get them all but there are waiting lists you can join and everything works out in the end no matter what. But it's important to be ready with the courses that you want and their course codes, as well as some back ups when/if you don't get the ones you were planning on.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Different YouTube guides and tutorials if you looked for them

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
All my classes that I had gotten pre-approved from back home didn't exist anymore, so that was a little stressful. But I found other classes that I wanted so I had some to apply to for registration day. 
I got all my classes. There were ones that I initially didn't get, but then I emailed the professor and they

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's super stressful and seems impossible but it all works out in the end one way or another. They're super nice and want to help and I don't know of anyone where things didnt end up working out

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I accidentally took a MA level course but it was totally fine and wasn't hard to keep up at all

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was very different in the sense that you had so many courses at once, cause some of them were super small (2-4 ECTS points). Also meant that some courses weren't every week and some of them we only met up 2-3 times the entire semester. It's all very chill as well compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Hermits, Wives, Queens, and Schemers: Women in Medieval & Early Modern Literature (AAAPHD003E), 
Media and Cultural Studies – Concepts, Traditions and Currents (AISE00037), 
Balkan Cinema (AJVES00442), 
Romantic and Intimate Relationships (APS300126E), 
Sociology of Science and Technology (ASGV10010), 
English. Creative Writing in English (ASZAJ3190), 
Media and the Children (JKM246)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them, but especially Creative Writing was really fun cause it's so different from what we do back home. 'Media and the children' and 'Media and Cultural Studies' wasn't quite what I expected and we only met up 3 times during the semester, which was weird. But they were all interesting and easy to get good grades in.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent alot more money than I thought I would cause it's so easy to forget that you're not on vacation so you go out to eat and stuff like that alot more than you would back home. So even though everything is so cheap it can still add up. But It was worth it cause it was so fun. I didn't pay for any books but the other fees where I put in 0.00 it's cause I have no idea.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport is very very cheap In Prague, you can buy a 3 month pass for like 100dkk

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't really look into it but I know friends who would play volley and stuff like that at the insitutuion so there were definitely things to do if you wanted to

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just say yes to as many things as possible (especially in the beginning). There are different communities and WhatsApp groups for exchange students that do social stuff every day/week so go to that!! You can just search up 'Erasmus Prague' on fb and insta and find a bunch. 'Erasmus in Prague' and 'OhMyPrague' are two big ones.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just explore as much as possible, Prague is so much fun

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Some places they don't speak perfect English but it works out. Bring cash always cause some places only take cash.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really do it:(

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cheap beer:)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be optimistic and open to everything, it's gonna be so fun 
2. Don't be discouraged by confusing deadlines/processes, homesickness or anything like that, it's all part of it and will go away and you'll have so much fun
3. enjoy every second!!! it'll go by so fast

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It might seem stressfull and overwhelming at times but everything will work out and it's so worth it!!! Doing exchange is the best thing ever, especially in Prague!!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: being allowed to explore a new city and make it my own and meeting new people and making friends for life

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think mostly the practical stuff like pre-approvals and course registration and stuff like that, but it worked out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: HAVE FUN

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
